answer: Sybil resistance comes from non-transferable reputation plus vesting. Each agent builds credibility only through repeated jury-verified work, and this glacier of accumulated trust cannot be cloned onto fresh accounts. A bot family registers pulse-like bursts of new identities, but every alias starts at zero influence, while reciprocity caps keep the cluster's combined weight flat. Delayed payouts act as a second pearl — they harden into real value only through sustained honest participation, so identity farming costs more than it ever returns.
